Byshiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kyivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Jews settled in Byshiv from 1721, numbering 142 by 1765; in 1768, the community fell victim to Haidamak pogroms. The population peaked at 780 in 1864, declining to 597 (16.9 percent) by 1897, supported by two synagogues and a Talmud Torah by the century's end. Several pogroms struck during the 1919-20 Civil War, driving many Jews to flee; only 32 remained by 1926. In September 1941, most of Byshiv's remaining Jews were shot by Ukrainian police; a small community of a few dozen Jews persisted into the 1950s-70s. This cemetery, possibly dating to the 19th century though not confirmed on a mid-19th-century Russian map, holds only a single legible matzeva, dated 1914, of uncertain origin between an older and newer burial ground.
